**How the step scales with the case.** On one GPU, from 100,000 tokens per case up, ISLA's memory grows linearly in
the number of tokens, as slice attention's $\mathcal{O}(NM)$ cost predicts, and so does its step time on the surface
task; on the volume task its step grows faster. @fig-cost-sweep measures both for every reference configuration, and
@tbl-cost-slopes gives what a token costs each of them.

## The switches {#sec-arch-switches}

**The class has one frame, one routing form, one length unit and one wall
geometry, and a short list of keyword-only arguments: the four field
declarations, the task, the role of the prediction points, the three
sizes, one compile knob and the spatial dimension.** @tbl-arch-switches
reads each default from the constructor's signature; the behavior that is
not an argument is described in the stages above.

```{python}
#| label: tbl-arch-switches
#| output: asis
WHAT = {
    "output_schema": ("5", "the output fields by name and rank spec (`{pressure: {rank: 0}, wss: {rank: 1}, stress: {rank: 2, symmetric: true}}`; `parity: odd` for a pseudotensor); each costs the coefficients of @tbl-arch-coeffs and is returned as a leaf of the output Mesh's `point_data` under its name. A dotted name (`surface.pressure`) is a nested leaf, in the output and in every input mapping"),
    "boundary_schemas": ("2, 3d", "per-cell fields of rank 0 to 2, read from every boundary mesh's `cell_data`: their invariants join the seed (prediction-point tokens carry zeros), and rank-1 and rank-2 fields add their contractions with $\\hat\\rho_{is}$ to the relational invariants"),
    "query_schema": ("interior", "per-prediction-point fields of rank 0 to 2, read from the prediction Mesh's `point_data` and carried by the prediction-point tokens through their own embedding after the built-in wall distance; rank-0 fields are lengths, divided by $L$ and paired with a signed log; requires `interior=True`"),
    "global_schema": ("1, 2, 3d, 5", "per-case fields of rank 0 or 1, read from `global_data` by name: each rank-1 field is a global direction $\\hat g_k$ (one seed cosine, one relational cosine, two basis vectors); each rank-0 field widens the seed"),
    "interior": ("modes", "the task: `False` predicts at the boundary cells and takes no prediction points; `True` predicts at the prediction points, which join the slice layers as tokens with the built-in wall geometry (@sec-arch-modes)"),
    "query_independent": ("modes, after each layer", "interior task only: `True` is ISLA-DTT, with read-only prediction points (no routing mass) that read the boundary cells through the forest at $\\theta = 1$ after every slice layer (@sec-arch-passive-decoder); rank-2 per-token inputs are refused with it"),
    "boundary_tokens": ("modes", "interior task only: the number of boundary tokens per case, drawn inside the model from the full-resolution boundary (the budget water-filled over the conditions, each cell drawn with probability proportional to its measure, each kept cell carrying its Horvitz-Thompson measure); a surface task takes the default"),
    "hidden": ("all", "the width $D$"),
    "n_layers": ("3", "the number of slice layers"),
    "n_slices": ("3, 4", "the slice count $M$ of every layer and of the head frame"),
    "compile_blocks": ("3", "run each slice block's forward under `torch.compile`, built lazily at the first call; parameter names, the state dict and the eager path are unchanged, and the fused geometry kernel stays a custom-op leaf. The way to compile ISLA-DTT, whose boundary read breaks the whole-model graph (@sec-arch-cost)"),
    "dim": ("all", "the spatial dimension: every boundary mesh is a `Mesh[dim - 1, dim]` (a polyline in two dimensions), every prediction point has `dim` coordinates, and the head's basis follows it (perpendiculars instead of cross products in two dimensions; odd-parity outputs refused for `dim >= 4`). A planar problem is passed with `dim=2`, never embedded with a zero third coordinate"),
}
sig = inspect.signature(ISLA.__init__).parameters
out = "| argument (default) | stage | what it sets |\n|:--------|:--|:----------------------------|\n"
for name in [n for n in sig if n != "self"]:
    dflt = sig[name].default
    dtxt = "required" if dflt is inspect.Parameter.empty else f"`{dflt!r}`"
    stage, what = WHAT[name]
    out += f"| `{name}` ({dtxt}) | {stage} | {what} |\n"
assert set(WHAT) == set(sig) - {"self"}
import physicsnemo.experimental.models.isla.geo_kernel as GK
out += (f"| `geo_kernel` attribute (`{REF.geo_kernel!r}`) | 3 | not an argument and not stored in a checkpoint: how the geometry region "
        f"runs, never what it computes. `\"auto\"` resolves at the first forward pass to the fused kernel when the inputs are on "
        f"CUDA, Triton is importable, `dim == 3`, there is at least one global direction, the global directions and rank-1 "
        f"per-token vectors number at most {GK.MAX_DIRECTIONS}, there are at most {GK.MAX_SLICES:,} slices and no rank-2 "
        f"per-token input, and to the eager region otherwise (`resolve_geo_kernel`); set `\"eager\"` or `\"fused\"` to force one |\n")
print(out)
print(": The constructor's keyword-only arguments, each default read from `inspect.signature(ISLA.__init__)` as the page "
      "renders, and the one execution attribute. How to read this: `hidden`, `n_layers` and `n_slices` default to the reference "
      "configuration; every other default is the surface task with no declared inputs.")
```
